questions.q: What problem does Kafka Connect exist to solve, per this lesson?
options: Providing a replacement for consumer groups
Replacing the need for topics and partitions entirely
Common integrations that thousands of teams solve identically, without each one writing a custom producer or consumer
Enforcing schema compatibility between producers and consumers
questions.explain: Connect targets the common case — moving data in and out of well-known systems — via configuration instead of custom client code.

questions.q: What is the difference between a source connector and a sink connector?
options: A source connector pulls data from an external system into a Kafka topic; a sink connector pushes data from a topic into an external system
A sink connector can only be used with compacted topics
There is no functional difference between the two
A source connector only reads from Kafka; a sink connector only writes to Kafka
questions.explain: Source connectors bring data in; sink connectors send data out — the two directions cover every Connect connector.

questions.q: In the example connector config in this lesson, what does connector.class control?
options: Whether the connector uses JSON or Avro serialization
Which specific connector implementation the worker should load and run
How long messages are retained in the destination topic
The partition key used for outgoing messages
questions.explain: connector.class names the specific connector implementation (e.g. a Debezium Postgres source connector) for the worker to run.

questions.q: What does tasks.max control in a Connect connector's configuration?
options: The maximum number of Kafka topics the connector can write to
How much of that connector's work can run in parallel
How many brokers the connector's Kafka cluster must have
The number of schema versions the connector can register
questions.explain: tasks.max sets the level of parallelism for that connector's work across Connect workers.

questions.q: What does the Confluent Cloud screenshot in this lesson actually show?
options: A real search of Confluent Cloud's connector catalog, looking for an available pre-built connector
A diagram illustrating how source and sink connectors differ conceptually
A code editor showing custom producer code
The Kafka broker configuration screen
questions.explain: It's a genuine screenshot of searching the real connector catalog, not an illustration of the source/sink concept.
